subject: Request: Temporary SLA amendment for async batch completion (retention & idempotency plan)
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme-retail.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
Cc: Akshay Gupta <akshay@retainer-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Nightly batch SLAs — ask for temporary completion window extension

Hi Stephanie,

Quick note from our ops team after the last two nightly runs: a subset of large catalog reconciliation jobs are missing the 4-hour completion window we signed up for. This only affects our busiest nights (1–2% of nightly batches) and causes downstream reconciliation timeouts.

We spoke with Akshay and he suggested asking Redwood for a temporary SLA amendment that:
- Extends the completion window for affected async jobs from 4 hours to 8 hours for the next 90 days while we migrate to smaller shards, and
- Provides firm guidance on retries and an idempotency approach we can implement to prevent duplicates during safe retries.

Can you share a proposed amendment and any operational mitigations Redwood can commit to (KV cache warmup, temporary increased burst capacity, or a retry/circuit policy)? We need to present this to our procurement/legal by Friday.

Thanks,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Data Platforms, ACME Retail

Attachments: run-log-sample-1123.txt (text)
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Akshay Gupta <akshay@retainer-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Nightly batch SLAs — ask for temporary completion window extension

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear summary and the log sample. We can absolutely work with you on a temporary amendment while you transition to smaller shards.

High level we can offer: 
- A 90-day carveout extending the async job completion SLO from 4h -> 8h for identified job classes (up to 3 job signatures you provide). This will include a label-based routing rule so only those jobs get the extended window.
- A documented safe-retry policy: Redwood will accept idempotency tokens (incoming header X-Redwood-Idempotency) with a 7-day TTL for these job classes; our runtime will do best-effort de-duplication for tokens present. We will also provide guidance for conditional ack semantics to minimize duplicate downstream processing.
- Operational mitigations during the 90-day window: temporary 20% burst capacity (subject to available pool) and a recommended KV cache pre-warm run during the 2 hours before the nightly window starts.

I will draft the amendment language and run the technical details by the infra team; copying Akshay for visibility. Expect a draft by Monday EOD. If procurement needs language earlier, tell me what minimum they need and I can fast-track.

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Nightly batch SLAs — ask for temporary completion window extension

Team — forwarding ACME's request. Key asks: 90-day extension 4h->8h for a small set of job signatures; idempotency guidance + 7-day TTL for tokens; 20% temporary burst if available; KV pre-warm guidance.

Questions for design:
1) Idempotency model: current runtime supports idempotency tokens for RPC-level dedupe for 24h. Can we extend TTL to 7 days for labelled jobs? What are memory/metadata implications?
2) Retry semantics: recommend at-least-once with client-supplied idempotency token, and server-side dedupe on token if present — but we need to confirm behavior for partially-successful multi-shard jobs.
3) Routing: can we implement label-based routing to apply the 8h policy only to specific job signatures?

Please reply with concise tradeoffs; I'll consolidate into the amendment draft.

Thanks,
— Stephanie
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T10:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Nightly batch SLAs — ask for temporary completion window extension

Stephanie — quick answers from infra/serving side: 

1) Idempotency TTL: We can increase the idempotency token retention for labelled jobs to 7 days, but it requires a small metadata shard extension. Expected impact: ~3–5% additional memory pressure on metadata nodes for customers using the feature at scale. We'll gate it behind a label so only ACME's class hits it.

2) Partial/sharded jobs: For multi-shard jobs we currently store per-job token + per-shard outcome. Safe de-duplication requires the client to present a single global idempotency token (recommended) and allow the server to return a consolidated final state. We'll document the recommended pattern: global token at job submission + idempotent downstream ingestion hooks. Edge case: if a shard times out and is retried independently, dedupe is best-effort (we'll mark retries in the job status). For full guarantees we'd need transactional cross-shard commit, which is out of scope for the temporary amendment.

3) Label-based routing: trivial — we have policy flags to match by job_tag or job_signature. We'll add a routing policy that maps matched jobs to the extended 8h completion SLO and the idempotency retention override.

Operational mitigations: we can offer a one-time 20% burst (subject to pool), and recommend a cache pre-warm script (we'll provide the script and a run checklist). We'll also provide a retry matrix with suggested backoffs and max attempts to minimize duplicate work (attached).

Ben — any billing or contractual concerns with temporary leniency on SLOs or with the idempotency window?

— Priyom
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-27T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Nightly batch SLAs — ask for temporary completion window extension

Quick note from commercial side: temporary amendment is ok from a billing perspective. Proposed commercial guardrails:
- The carveout applies to up to 3 job signatures and stays active for a single 90-day window (non-renewing unless mutually agreed).
- If the extended window is abused (more than 5% of total nightly job volume over 2 weeks), Redwood reserves the right to revoke burst capacity and revert to normal SLOs.
- No change to base pricing; any sustained increased utilization beyond burst will be billed at standard overage rates.

I'll draft the commercial paragraph and include the revoke clause. After we agree, legal can finalize and we'll attach an amendment PDF for signature.

— Ben

Subject: Re: Nightly batch SLAs — ask for temporary completion window extension

Hi Sofia — attaching a short amendment and an operations appendix for your review. Summary of commitments: 
- 90-day temporary SLA amendment: completion window for agreed job signatures extended to 8 hours.
- Idempotency: Redwood will accept X-Redwood-Idempotency header with a 7-day TTL for labelled jobs; server will perform best-effort dedupe and return consolidated job state. See appendix for recommended client pattern.
- Operational mitigations: one-time 20% burst capacity allocation (subject to pool availability) + KV pre-warm script and checklist.
- Commercial guardrails: carveout applies to up to 3 job signatures; abuse clause and overage billing described in attached amendment.

Next steps: Please confirm the three job signatures you want in scope and we will issue the DocuSign amendment (link below). Once signed, we'll schedule the pre-warm run and provide the idempotency-spec appendix.

DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/ACME-SLA-REDW-2026

Thanks,
— Stephanie
